mechanism_narrative: A rising FEDFUNDS rate above 5.5% in the current month signals a tightening cycle that reduces future discounting of equities, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat when FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.5%, with t-statistic > 1.96 over 50 such events.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) by at least 2% coinciding with a decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests labor market strengthening, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2% AND UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when the trigger occurs (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in GDPC1 (real personal consumption) of 3% for two consecutive months predicts increased future equity demand, leading to positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by ≥3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the consumption momentum (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 100 for three consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which is associated with negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the contraction (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4% for three consecutive months, the low-rate environment is expected to persist, supporting higher equity valuations and positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when the low-rate condition ends (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 3.5% followed by a rise in HOUST (housing starts) suggests improving labor market conditions and housing optimism, predicting positive 60-day forward returns.
regime_hint: labor market improving with housing momentum
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when the trigger occurs.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in CPIAUCSL above 0.3% indicate accelerating inflation, which is expected to erode equity valuations and produce negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when inflation accelerates (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in RSAFS (retail sales) of 5% or more over four months indicates weakening consumer demand, which typically precedes negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by ≥5% over four consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative when the decline ends (p > 0.05).
